sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed at 7,743 on Sep 25, within 0.3% of its one-month high of 7,765 and about 2.5% above its one-month low. The Nasdaq 100 sits just as close to its own one-month high (30,608 vs. a 30,732 ceiling), also comfortably clear of its 28,938 floor. The VIX is at 14.87, well off its one-month high of 17.84, consistent with a market pricing in limited event risk. The Euro Stoxx 50 remains the outlier, running about 2.8% below its one-month high of 6,486. Against that calm backdrop, only 6 operating names across the SP500/R1000/core-coverage universe report this week, with consumer-defensive names making up half the calendar alongside single reports from technology, industrials and materials.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tue: LW US and STZ US both report into consumer-defensive, this week's largest reporting cohort at -0.54% median across 379 names. Tue: RPM US reports into materials, a quieter group at -0.39% median across 545 names. Thu: APLD US reports into technology, the strongest positive mover among this week's reporting sectors at +0.84% median. Fri: DAL US closes the week in industrials, the most reactive reporting sector at -1.42% median across 651 names.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining leads the sector reaction table at a median +6.62% across 178 names, backed by a thick 2,630-item news window. Alternative-asset-management (+2.93%, 6 tickers, 241 items) and copper (+2.63%, 6 tickers, 248 items) follow, though both run thin news coverage for small groups. None of the three has an event this week; among sectors actually reporting, industrials is the most reactive at -1.42% across 651 names.
